# ReentrantReadWriteLock

`ReentrantReadWriteLock` separates access to shared state into a shared read
lock and an exclusive write lock. This example uses both to protect a bank
account while twelve balance reads and two withdrawals are submitted.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this example, attendees can:

- distinguish shared reading from exclusive writing and explain the visibility
  guarantee between the write and read locks;
- explain why a withdrawal rechecks the balance under the write lock; and
- discuss scheduling, fairness and performance trade-offs without treating a
  sample trace as a guarantee.

## Prerequisite

Install an
[Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8) JDK
or newer, and ensure `java` and `javac` resolve to it in the terminal.

## The program to inspect

`BankAccount` protects `balance` with a read-write lock. A single
mutual-exclusion lock, such as `synchronized` or `ReentrantLock`, could protect
the same state, but would also exclude other readers. Here multiple threads may
hold the read lock together; a writer needs exclusive access. Each successful
acquisition is paired with an `unlock()` in a `finally` block.

`withdraw()` first checks the balance under the read lock, releases it, then
acquires the write lock and checks again before updating. Another withdrawal
could change the balance between those acquisitions. The second check and update
form one exclusive operation; the first check and the update do not. Without
consistent locking, concurrent withdrawals could overwrite one another or act on
stale state.

```java
static final class BankAccount {

    private final ReentrantReadWriteLock lock = new ReentrantReadWriteLock();
    /* Protected by the ReentrantReadWriteLock lock */
    private BigDecimal balance;

    BankAccount(final BigDecimal initialBalance) {
        this.balance = requirePositive(initialBalance);
    }

    public void withdraw(final BigDecimal amount) {
        requirePositive(amount);

        lock.readLock().lock(); /* Acquire the lock to safely read the balance */
        try {
            log("Read log acquired");
            final BigDecimal newBalance = balance.add(amount.negate());
            if (isNegative(newBalance)) {
                log("There is not enough money (" + balance + ") to cover the withdrawal (" + amount + ')');
                return;
            }
        } finally {
            log("Releasing the read lock");
            lock.readLock().unlock();
        }

        /* ReentrantReadWriteLock does not support upgrading from the read lock to the write lock: a thread that
            holds a read lock and then requests the write lock waits indefinitely. Release the read lock first,
            but revalidate the state after acquiring the write lock because another thread may change it. A thread
            that holds the write lock can acquire the read lock and then release the write lock to downgrade. */
        lock.writeLock().lock();
        try {
            log("Write log acquired");
            /* Another thread may have updated the value once the read lock was released */
            final BigDecimal newBalanceBeforeWrite = balance.add(amount.negate());
            if (isNegative(newBalanceBeforeWrite)) {
                log("There is not enough money (" + balance + ") to cover the withdrawal (" + amount + ')');
                return;
            }

            log("Withdrawing " + amount + " from " + balance);
            balance = newBalanceBeforeWrite;
            log("New balance after withdrawal " + balance);
        } finally {
            log("Releasing the write lock");
            lock.writeLock().unlock();
        }
    }

    public BigDecimal balance() {
        lock.readLock().lock(); /* Acquire the lock to safely read the balance */
        try {
            return balance;
        } finally {
            lock.readLock().unlock(); /* Release the lock */
        }
    }
}
```

Both locks are reentrant. A thread holding only the read lock cannot upgrade to
the write lock: calling `writeLock().lock()` while retaining the read lock will
not succeed. Release the read lock first and revalidate under the write lock. A
write-lock holder can instead acquire the read lock before releasing the write
lock, thereby downgrading without an intervening writer. This example does not
perform a downgrade.

The Java Memory Model defines visibility and ordering for shared state. The
`ReadWriteLock` contract ensures that a successful read-lock acquisition sees
updates made before a previous release of its associated write lock: that
release happens-before the subsequent read-lock acquisition. Thus a protected
balance read after that acquisition sees the withdrawal or a subsequent
protected update. Write-lock releases and subsequent write-lock acquisitions
also have lock memory-synchronisation effects. These guarantees are distinct
from the write lock’s mutual exclusion, which protects the check and update.

The default lock is non-fair: acquisition order is unspecified and sustained
contention can indefinitely postpone readers or writers. Fair mode offers an
approximately arrival-order policy, with its own trade-offs. Shared reads may
improve throughput for suitable workloads, but short reads, locking overhead and
contention can outweigh the benefit. Measure the actual workload; this example
is not a benchmark.

The tasks use `CompletableFuture.runAsync` as launching scaffolding. It normally
uses the common pool, with a thread-per-task fallback if the pool cannot support
parallelism of at least two. `allOf(...).join()` waits for them before the final
balance read. With the initial balance of 1200 and two withdrawals of 100,
normal completion leaves 1000. Individual reads can observe 1200, 1100 or 1000
depending on scheduling; their order and overlapping execution are not
guaranteed.

## Guided walkthrough

Run these commands from the `examples/reentrant-read-write-lock` directory.
Choose one of the following ways to run the example.

1. Run the example using the
   [Maven `exec` plugin](https://www.mojohaus.org/exec-maven-plugin/).

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean compile exec:exec
   ```
